sam (eng-runtime): Heads-up — after the v2.3.1 rollout we're seeing OOM spikes for long-context workloads (seqlen > 2k). I put the rollout on hold.
claire (eng-ml): ugh, saw a couple alerts. Is this the kernel-router change from this morning?
sam (eng-runtime): likely. The merged patch changed the eviction annealing schedule + kernel fastpath scoring. Memory looks like it balloons when requests pick the new fastpath kernels with pinned kv slices.
ryan (eng-runtime): can you paste the top of the OOM logs?
sam (eng-runtime): pasted below — repeating pattern where a single inference goes from ~4.2GB -> 12.6GB in <200ms and then OOM.
```
[2026-03-18T10:12:03Z] request id=abc-123 model=redwood-8k seqlen=2500 kernel=fastpath-v2 alloc=12.6GB OOM
[2026-03-18T10:12:06Z] process pid=4321 killed by OOM after kv-slab-alloc failure
```
claire (eng-ml): that sequence-length sensitivity matches the local repro I ran. If we force the old kernel selector, memory stays stable.
deepak (eng-infra): CI perf bot also flagged a regression on the throughput benchmark last night — ~7% drop on token/sec for short prompts while mem usage for long prompts increased. perf-bot, any links?
perf-bot: perf summary: https://perf.internal/reports/2026-03-18/rollout-v2.3.1 — p50 latency unchanged, p95 +2%, token/s -7% on small-batch microbench, mem +30% on longctx tests.
ryan (eng-runtime): ok can we bisect to the exact commit? I started a local bisect: the bad range is between commit 6f3b9e (batcher heuristics) and abc1234 (kernel-router scoring).
sam (eng-runtime): ran git bisect, landed on commit abc1234 — changes: eviction annealing params and kernel weight calc. Reverting just the anneal patch locally removes the OOMs.
```
# simplified repro steps
git checkout abc1234
./scripts/run_longctx_repro.sh --model redwood-8k --seqlen 2500 --concurrency 1
# observe OOM
```
liz (oncall): rolling a partial revert now on one host pool to confirm. Oncall note: if you adjust eviction threshold make sure we don't regress latency.
claire (eng-ml): curious: why would kernel fastpath cause higher memory? Are we duplicating KV caches per kernel instance?
ryan (eng-runtime): yes — the fastpath instantiates short-lived per-request kv views that aren't being compacted immediately due to the anneal schedule — small slabs accumulate and fragment. For long prompts that translates into huge resident set.
deepak (eng-infra): can we add a temporary mitigation: force kernel routing to prefer the legacy kernel for seqlen>1024 and nudge eviction to immediate compact on slab count > 128?
sam (eng-runtime): I pushed a runtime flag to the config service: kernel.router.override=legacy_if_seqlen_gt:1024 and kv.evict.immediate_on_slab_count=128. Applying to canaries now.
```
# runtime curl
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://config.internal/runtime/flags -d '{"kernel.router.override":"legacy_if_seqlen_gt:1024"}'
```
deploy-bot: rollout paused -> canary update applied to pool:longctx-canary (3 nodes).
liz (oncall): canaries look stable after override. Memory back to baseline on those hosts. Monitoring for 30m.
claire (eng-ml): for the postmortem / fix: we should separate kernel scoring changes from eviction heuristics in future PRs — they're orthogonal but interacted badly. Also add a longctx perf job to CI (seqlen 2048+).
ryan (eng-runtime): agreed. I'll open a revert PR for the annealing change and a follow-up that splits changes and adds the longctx CI test. Also capturing heap profiles: https://profiles.internal/heap/2167504321 (sample).
sam (eng-runtime): thanks — marking this thread rollout-blocker. Will update when revert merges. :thumbsup:
liz (oncall): if anyone sees new OOM alerts ping me directly.
deploy-bot: revert PR created: runtime:revert/evict-anneal-abc1234 -> https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4321
ryan (eng-runtime): perf note: when we reintroduce kernel scoring, let's add an explicit check for per-kernel kv-alloc delta in the perf gate to prevent silent memory regressions.
sam (eng-runtime): ack, will include that in the PR checklist.
